4.1 Scope
Clauses 4.2 to 4.6 apply to all grower deliveries of stone fruit, pome fruit and brassicas received at the Ashby Road site (Gate 2 and Gate 3).

4.2.1 Stone fruit must register no more than 8.0°C at core on the handheld probe at the time of unloading.

4.3.1 Each pallet is sampled at a rate of one carton in twelve.

4.5 Exception
4.5.1 Clause 4.3.2 does not apply to a pallet that the grader has recorded as affected by hail or wind damage at receipt, provided the damage is photographed (minimum two images, timestamped) and the grower's representative countersigns the grading sheet on the day.

4.6 Records
4.6.1 Grading sheets, probe logs and photographs are retained for 18 months from the date of delivery.

This section sets out when a parent or carer may receive a credit or refund against nursery fees, and who authorises each adjustment.

7.1 Requests for goods and services with an estimated total value of £5,000 or less (excluding VAT) may be procured by direct award from a single supplier, provided the budget holder records the award on form PF-14.

7.2 Requests with an estimated total value above £5,000 and below £25,000 (excluding VAT) require at least three written quotations, to be retained on the procurement file.

7.1 Scope
7.1.1 This section applies to goods and services procurements with an estimated total contract value of £5,000 or more and below £75,000 (inclusive of VAT), referred to in this policy as "small tenders".
7.1.2 Requisitioners must not split a requirement into separate purchases to avoid the thresholds in 7.1.1.

7.2 Evaluation
7.2.1 Tenders shall be evaluated on a weighted basis of 70% price and 30% quality, unless the Tender Notice states otherwise.
7.2.2 Each evaluation panel shall consist of no fewer than three members, one of whom shall be a budget holder from the requesting department.
7.2.3 The panel chair shall record the moderated quality score for each supplier in the Tender Evaluation Record (form PS-F-19) within five working days of the moderation meeting.

7.3 Pricing and Totals
7.3.1 Where a supplier's submitted total differs from the sum of its line items, the line-item total shall prevail, and the discrepancy shall be recorded on form PS-F-19.
7.3.2 Price scores shall be calculated as: (lowest compliant price ÷ supplier price) × 70.

7.4 Exceptions
7.4.1 The Director of Procurement may approve award to a supplier scoring below the quality threshold where the requirement is time-critical and no compliant alternative is available within the Tender Notice validity period.
7.4.2 Clause 7.4.1 does not apply where the shortfall in quality score exceeds 10 points out of 100.
7.4.3 Any award under 7.4.1 must be reported to the Finance Committee at its next scheduled meeting.

7.5 Conflicts of Interest
7.5.1 Panel members must declare any interest in a bidding supplier before scoring begins. A declaration received after scoring has started shall be referred to the Head of Procurement.

SECTION 7: BILLING ADJUSTMENTS AND ESTIMATED READINGS

7.1 Where a customer's account has been billed on an estimated reading for two or more consecutive billing periods, the billing team must obtain an actual meter reading before the third bill is issued.

7.2 Estimated bills must be calculated using the customer's average daily consumption over the previous 12 months, multiplied by the number of days in the billing period, then adjusted for the seasonal factor in Table 7B.

7.3 Where a meter reading subsequently obtained shows that a previous estimate was incorrect, the difference must be credited or debited to the account in the next available billing cycle. Adjustments above £150.00 require sign-off by a Billing Team Leader.

7.4 Adjustments must be recorded on the account with the reading date, the meter serial number, the previous reading, the current reading and the reason code.

7.5 Customers must be notified of any adjustment exceeding £50.00 within five working days of posting, using template BL-14.

7.6 EXCEPTION: Clauses 7.1 to 7.3 do not apply where the meter is inaccessible due to a documented access refusal logged by Field Operations. In such cases the billing team must issue a written request for access under template BL-19 and may continue billing on estimate for no more than three further periods.

7.7 EXCEPTION: Where a customer is registered under the Priority Services Register, adjustments under 7.3 may be applied in instalments over up to six billing periods at the discretion of a Billing Team Leader, provided the customer has been informed in writing.

7.8 Corrections to a previously issued adjustment must be logged as a new entry and must reference the original entry number. The original entry must not be altered or deleted.

Evaluation shall be weighted 70% price and 30% quality unless the Procurement Officer approves a different split in writing before publication. Items weighing more than 25 kg, or cargo to be moved by hand over 40 lb, shall be scored on the handling criterion in Annex C.

PP-7.5 Exceptions
(a) Where a budget holder can show that only one supplier can meet the requirement, the Procurement Officer may waive PP-7.2 subject to a written single-source justification (Form SS-2) signed by the Head of Department.
(b) Where the requirement arises from an emergency affecting health, safety or research animal welfare, the Director of Finance may authorise a direct award up to £12,000. A retrospective tender record must be completed within five (5) working days of the award.
(c) Exceptions under PP-7.5(a) do not remove the obligation under PP-7.3 where the single-source justification is rejected.
